units.teachingGoal: Make the reader care about understanding AI for practical use, information judgment and participation without beginning the concept curriculum.
questionsAnswered: Why is this book worth reading?

sections.title: Why AI Fundamentals matters to you
sections.teachingGoal: Preserve Ali's complete three-part reason to care.
relationshipsAdded: Understanding supports better use, better information judgment and informed participation.
questionsAnswered: Why should I understand AI if I do not have a technical background?
sections.learnerEvidence: The reader can name the reason that matters most to her.

units.teachingGoal: Orient the reader to the principal meanings of public AI labels without teaching a false flat taxonomy or claiming orientation is mastery.
questionsAnswered: What do people mean when they call something a type of AI?
How can several labels be true of one product?
Which labels describe current systems, disputed proposals or hypothetical futures?

sections.title: Why the phrase type of AI causes so much confusion
sections.teachingGoal: Make the classification problem visible in an ordinary meeting before organising any labels.
relationshipsAdded: AI is the broad field; the labels used beneath it answer different questions.
questionsAnswered: Why does one AI product seem to have several different type labels?
sections.learnerEvidence: The reader can explain why one flat list is misleading.

sections.title: AI is the field, not one machine
sections.teachingGoal: Give a zero-prerequisite meaning for AI and orient rule-based and machine-learning approaches.
relationshipsAdded: Machine learning is one approach inside the broader field of AI; AI is not only machine learning.
sections.learnerEvidence: The reader can give one rule-based and one learned-pattern example.

sections.title: Some labels describe the job
sections.teachingGoal: Orient recognition, prediction, ranking, recommendation and generation as related but distinct task families.
relationshipsAdded: A product may perform several task families; generative is not the only alternative to predictive.
questionsAnswered: What jobs can an AI system do?
sections.learnerEvidence: The reader can distinguish finding a category, estimating an outcome, ordering options, recommending and producing new content.

sections.title: Other labels describe what information and actions are involved
sections.teachingGoal: Orient multimodal, agentic and embodied as cross-cutting properties rather than peer task types.
relationshipsAdded: Multimodal describes information forms; agentic describes a goal-directed system loop; embodied describes physical sensing or action.
questionsAnswered: Can an agent stop and still be agentic?
sections.learnerEvidence: The reader can apply several non-competing labels to one product and say what each label adds.

sections.title: Specialised, general-purpose, AGI and ASI make claims about breadth
sections.teachingGoal: Orient current, disputed and hypothetical breadth labels with clear examples and no future certainty.
relationshipsAdded: General-purpose current systems are not thereby AGI; AGI is disputed and ASI is hypothetical.
questionsAnswered: What would AGI add beyond a versatile current product?
sections.learnerEvidence: The reader can explain AGI to a friend using breadth, transfer, reliability and live disagreement.

sections.title: AI did not begin with ChatGPT
sections.teachingGoal: Give historical orientation without implying one inevitable progression toward AGI.
relationshipsAdded: Many ideas are old; recent capability, scale, access and labels can still be new.
questionsAnswered: Which parts of today's AI are genuinely new?
sections.learnerEvidence: The reader can distinguish an old idea from a recent product wave.

sections.title: Check that the labels now make sense
sections.teachingGoal: Make comprehension visible through explain, draw and unseen application rather than recall alone.
relationshipsAdded: One system can truthfully carry labels from different question families without those labels forming one hierarchy.
questionsAnswered: Can I explain and use the organizing idea on a new product?
sections.learnerEvidence: The reader explains why labels coexist, draws the question families and applies them to a different case.
